chapter_title: The Making of a Global World
storyboard: Pre-Modern: Silk Routes, spaghetti, smallpox biological conquest.
19th Century: Corn Laws, refrigerated ships, Rinderpest, indentured labor.
Inter-War: WWI industrial war, Henry Ford mass production, 1929 Great Depression.
Post-War: 1944 Bretton Woods (IMF/World Bank), G-77 NIEO, production relocation.
summary: Examines long-term global interconnectedness through trade flows, colonial expansion, economic crises, and international financial institutions.
key_takeaways: Pre-modern networks linked Asia, Europe, and Africa in trade and biological exchange.
19th-century trade was defined by flows of goods, labor, and capital under imperialism.
Bretton Woods established fixed exchange rates pegged to US Dollar.
Developing nations created G-77 to demand New International Economic Order.
